name: Kabsa (Chicken)
description: Fragrant saffron-spiced rice with slow-braised chicken, dried fruits, and fried onions — the national dish.

name: Kabsa (Lamb)
description: Whole lamb joint slow-cooked with aromatic Kabsa spice blend atop long-grain rice.

name: Jareesh
description: Cracked wheat slow-cooked to a creamy porridge with lamb, topped with crispy onions and ghee.

name: Saleeg
description: White rice simmered in milk broth with chicken; Hejazi comfort food served with tomato sauce.

name: Maraq Lamb Broth
description: Clear spiced lamb broth with herbs — traditionally the first course of a Saudi feast.

name: Machboos Rubyan (Shrimp Rice)
description: Gulf-style spiced rice with jumbo shrimp, dried limes (loomi), and rose water — beloved on the Red Sea coast.

name: Sayadiya Fish Rice
description: Levantine-influenced fish rice; caramelised onion gravy soaks into long-grain rice beneath whole grilled fish.

name: Thareed (Lamb Bread Stew)
description: Thin flat bread layered with slow-braised lamb and vegetables; the Prophet ﷺ's described as the best of foods.

name: Harees
description: Wheat and lamb pounded to a silky paste; simple, ancient, and deeply satisfying — especially during Ramadan.

name: Samboosa Platter
description: Crispy triangular pastries filled with spiced minced meat, herbs, and pine nuts.

name: Mandi (Slow-Roasted Lamb)
description: Whole lamb smoked low-and-slow in an underground pit (tandoor); the smoke flavour is unmistakable.

name: Madfoon (Buried Lamb)
description: Seasoned lamb buried in a sand pit with hot coals overnight; Najdi highland tradition at its finest.

name: Ouzi (Whole Lamb with Rice)
description: A whole roasted lamb on a bed of spiced rice, crowned with pine nuts and raisins — the ultimate celebration dish.

name: Mathbi Grilled Chicken
description: Spatchcocked chicken pressed between two hot stones over open coals — smoky, charred, and aromatic.

name: Mutabbaq (Filled Pancake)
description: Street-food pancake stuffed with egg, minced lamb, onion, and leek; a Jeddah Balad staple.

name: Lahm bil Basal (Lamb & Onion Stew)
description: Slow-braised lamb shanks with caramelised onions in a rich tomato base; served with flatbread.

name: Kabsa Dinner Special
description: Evening-edition kabsa with added dried apricots, almonds, and a darker, smokier spice profile.

name: Fish Mandi (Jeddah Style)
description: Red Sea fish smoked Mandi-style over wood embers with turmeric rice; a coastal flagship dish.

name: Shish Tawook Platter
description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken cubes charcoal-grilled on skewers; served with garlic toum and warm bread.

name: Kunafa bil Jibneh (Cheese Pastry)
description: Crispy shredded pastry over white cheese soaked in rose-water syrup; Levantine-influenced Hejazi dessert.
